title: Accurate Low-Degree Polynomial Approximation of Non-Polynomial Operators for Fast Private Inference in Homomorphic Encryption
problem: Non-polynomial operators such as activation functions cannot be directly computed in homomorphic encryption schemes, forcing private inference to rely on expensive polynomial approximations that degrade both speed and accuracy.
motivation: Private neural network inference via homomorphic encryption protects sensitive data and model parameters from untrusted servers, but computational cost of approximate operators is a critical bottleneck.
method: The paper proposes techniques for constructing low-degree polynomial approximations of non-polynomial operators (ReLU, sigmoid, etc.) that can be efficiently evaluated within homomorphic encryption. The approach optimizes the balance between polynomial degree and approximation error, enabling rapid evaluation of neural network layers on encrypted data.
key_novelty: A method to achieve accurate low-degree polynomial approximations of non-polynomial operators, significantly reducing the computational overhead of private inference in homomorphic encryption.
contributions: Systematic approach for approximating common non-polynomial neural network operators with low-degree polynomials
Analysis of approximation error bounds and accuracy-efficiency trade-offs
Demonstration of fast private inference using the approximation scheme
Empirical validation on CNN and transformer models with minimal accuracy loss

metrics.accuracy: minimal accuracy degradation from polynomial approximation

primary_theme: low-degree polynomial approximation for efficient private inference
